facts: state=(keys,values,offset), scalar offset counts consumed tokens
merge(caches) returns BatchKVCache; single cache has no extract/filter/prepare methods
trim(n) only adjusts offset and is not recurrent rollback
merge right-aligns historical KV with left padding; per-row offset equals real history length while _idx equals maximum history length
model inputs in equal-q bucket may share q with differing history lengths; RoPE reads per-row offset and causal mask excludes historical left padding
extract(idx) returns KVCache with historical left padding removed and contiguous keys/values; requires initialized tensors
filter(indices) mutates rows and may shift common historical padding; stable request/slot identity must be tracked outside cache
prepare(*,left_padding=None,lengths=None,right_padding=None); lengths ignored for KV; new left_padding only permitted on empty cache
finalize rolls right padding to historical left and adjusts offsets
state omits _right_padding: do not snapshot prepared/unfinalized padded state using state alone
trim(n) subtracts same n from all rows; cannot represent unequal accepted-prefix lengths
state=(cache,left_padding,lengths), no token offset and no trim implementation
merge concatenates initialized row states, fills missing rows with zero; all-empty merge sets zero left_padding
extract(idx) slices every cache tensor and drops lengths/left_padding; None tensor raises on slicing
prepare(lengths=None,**kwargs) converts lengths; it does not install left_padding from kwargs
advance(N) subtracts N from lengths/left_padding; finalize clears both
make_mask(N) combines left-padding and remaining-length masks; context length need not match across initialized row states
Masked recurrent updates preserve prior recurrent state, but convolution-state handling separately depends on lengths
Simply append zero or pad tokens without prepare/mask/finalize is not safe recurrent recovery
For right-padded input prepare(lengths=real_lengths,right_padding=pad_counts) before model; consume complete tensor then finalize before extract. Upstream generate.py:1221-1236 follows this protocol
Equal-q verification buckets need no new-input padding; historical KV left padding does not imply padding recurrent input

minimal_algorithm: Maintain single-row target and draft caches per stable request-id plus slot generation, fully initialized and finalized before merging.
Take independent original-row snapshot via audited CacheAdapter before speculative work. Merge matching layer caches into disposable bucket cache by exact q; run real model on [bucket_size,q].
q includes the current unconsumed token: propose at most q-1 drafts and verify [old_y,*draft]. Every row has at least q=1.
Use target greedy logits to accept contiguous matching draft prefix and one target replacement/bonus; apply output budget and first EOS before calculating consumed prefix.

On complete full acceptance adopt extracted target cache only if its consumed prefix is exactly [old_y,*actual[:-1]]. Otherwise restore original single-row cache and replay that exact consumed prefix.

Draft cache must independently reconcile its consumed prefix, including catch-up pending tokens; simplest correct control is restore original draft snapshot and replay old pending plus consumed tokens for every row.
On cancel/error discard disposable batch caches and leave original snapshots intact; do not publish partial cache or scheduler observations as completed work.
Record requested q, valid verified q, executed padded q, number of model forward submissions and end-to-end synchronized time. Forward call count is not Metal kernel count.
required_runtime_validation: dense and hybrid heterogeneous-context same-q bucket logits/output comparison
shared-cap padded control with per-row mask/finalize and same recovery
mixed rejection/full-accept plus EOS and remaining output budget 1
single-row cache prefix equality after replay and next-token equality
actual batch numeric divergence retained; source API review cannot prove bitwise equality or speed
